scenes.headline: How a grounding model writes boxes as tokens
scenes.sub: GroundingPI: points and boxes from one shared vocabulary
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Reticle! Ask a vision model where the mug is, and it must answer in numbers. This model answers in words made for the job.

scenes.text: Every coordinate is a single vocabulary entry, from <0> to <999>. A point is two tokens and a box is four.
scenes.say: The idea: every coordinate is one entry in the vocabulary, a thousand of them. A point is two tokens, and a box is four.

scenes.title: From pixels to a token string

steps.say: The image goes through the vision encoder from Kimi.
A small projector merges each two by two block of patches into one visual token.
A Qwen three decoder reads those tokens next to the question.
And it writes the answer token by token: a label, then its coordinates.

scenes.title: Snapping a coordinate to a token
scenes.say: Coordinates are scaled by the image size, then snapped onto the token grid.

parts.note: the coordinate on a grid of 0 to 1000
parts.say: First, a coordinate becomes a whole number between zero and a thousand.
Then it is squeezed onto the thousand tokens and rounded.
Q is the token the model writes. Decoding divides by nine hundred ninety-nine.

scenes.title: One answer, read off the page

steps.say: Here is a real answer. Two minions share one wrapper, their boxes separated by a comma.
The car isn't in the picture, so the model says None rather than staying silent.

items.say: First a general vision language model.
Then coordinate alignment, with plain cross entropy.
Last, reinforcement learning that rewards coverage, tight boxes and correct counts.

scenes.title: Mean of 11 capability scores
scenes.note: Astra still leads GUI clicking by 13.67
scenes.say: The headline average reproduces exactly from the paper's tables. It wins eight of eleven capabilities, but loses screen clicking badly.

scenes.text: Make coordinates part of the vocabulary, and a box costs four tokens instead of a sentence of digits.

recap: One token per coordinate, 1,000 of them
Kimi encoder, Qwen decoder, small projector
Strong average, but screens still lag
scenes.say: To recap: one token per coordinate, a borrowed encoder and decoder, and an average that holds up, with screens still behind.
